name: Blockchain Fundamentals
description: Foundational knowledge of what blockchain technology is, how it works structurally, and what problems it solves. Covers the definition and properties of blockchains, the principle of decentralization and its significance, the data structure (blocks, chains, Merkle trees), basic read/write operations, and real-world application domains. This is the entry point for all blockchain development work.

subskills.name: What is Blockchain
subskills.description: Definition and properties of a blockchain: an immutable, append-only distributed ledger of transactions grouped into cryptographically linked blocks. Covers the distinction between a blockchain and a traditional database, the public vs private vs consortium spectrum, permissioned vs permissionless networks, and why immutability is achieved through cryptographic hashing.

subskills.name: Decentralization & Why It Matters
subskills.description: The principle of distributing authority, data, and computation across many nodes with no single point of control or failure. Covers the blockchain trilemma (decentralization, security, scalability), censorship resistance, trust minimization, Byzantine fault tolerance, and the trade-offs between decentralization and performance.

subskills.name: Blockchain Structure
subskills.description: The data structures underlying a blockchain: block headers (previous hash, Merkle root, timestamp, nonce, difficulty target), transaction data, Merkle trees for efficient transaction verification, and the chain of hashes that ensures tamper evidence. Covers genesis block, block height, and how forks affect chain structure.

subskills.name: Basic Blockchain Operations
subskills.description: How transactions are created, signed, broadcast, validated, and included in blocks. Covers the transaction lifecycle (creation → mempool → mining/validation → confirmation), transaction fees (gas in Ethereum), confirmations and finality, wallet addresses and private/public key pairs, and reading blockchain data via block explorers.

subskills.name: Applications & Use Cases
subskills.description: Real-world domains where blockchain technology adds genuine value: decentralized finance (DeFi), supply chain provenance, digital identity and self-sovereign identity (SSI), tokenization of real-world assets (RWA), non-fungible tokens (NFTs), voting systems, healthcare data management, and cross-border payments. Understanding use-case fit vs hype is essential.

github.signal: README or documentation explaining blockchain fundamentals, architecture, or use cases
Block explorer integration, blockchain data reading scripts, or transaction parsing code

cv.signal: Demonstrated understanding of blockchain technology, distributed ledger systems, or decentralized architectures
Built or contributed to blockchain-based applications or proofs of concept

linkedin.signal: Blockchain, distributed ledger technology, or decentralization endorsed
DeFi, NFT, supply chain blockchain, or blockchain use cases mentioned

junior.description: Clearly explains what a blockchain is, why decentralization matters, can describe block structure and the transaction lifecycle from creation to confirmation.

mid.description: Critically evaluates blockchain use-case fit vs traditional database alternatives, articulates trilemma trade-offs for specific application domains.

senior.description: Advises organizations on blockchain adoption decisions, distinguishes genuine decentralization value from hype, and designs systems that respect the trilemma.
